title: Batch-Compare cDNA FASTA.GZ Samples for One Target Gene (CLI Tutorial)

graphics.caption: The native RNA-read Mapping workspace loads a persisted TP53 report and keeps phase-1 seed filtering separate from phase-2 alignment. In this bounded acceptance fixture all six retained reads align, while the seed-passed subset remains empty.

The native cohort view reports six target-assigned fragments but no full-length or direct-transition evidence. Target assignment therefore must not be reported as seed-filter acceptance, complete molecules, or junction support.

Transcript-oriented teaching diagram: 5′- and 3′-UTR reach begin at explicit CDS boundaries, while a clipped transcript-facing end remains a right-censored lower bound rather than becoming an exact short UTR.

Synthetic six-barcode Sample-2 comparison showing the primary regular-cDNA 16/15 shift as a solid point and the enriched 14/13 and 18/17 shifts as separate countercheck ticks across whole-read, 5′-UTR-control and 3′-UTR panels. This is a teaching fixture, not biological evidence.

catalog.notes: Hands-on batch workflow for interpreting many gzipped cDNA FASTA files, aligning saved reports, exporting one target-gene cohort sample sheet, and continuing into transcript-bound 5′/3′-UTR reach projection. The six-barcode teaching contrast keeps barcode16/15 as the primary regular-cDNA pair for Sample 2 and 14/13 plus 18/17 as separately prepared directional counterchecks. Native acceptance on 2026-10-01 used two bounded TP53 samples and explicitly separates seed filtering, alignment assignment, molecule completeness, direct-transition evidence and later synthetic read-end teaching assets.
